What I bring

  • I dig into the details

    I start up close with the data, learning how it was collected and where the gaps are. Then I step back to see the bigger picture.

  • I connect data to place

    Maps reveal patterns a spreadsheet can't. I use spatial analysis to tie data to the places where people live, work, and move.

  • I work across research and fieldwork

    I've knocked on 500+ doors, logged 50+ hours of interviews, and done dozens of field investigations alongside government, nonprofit, and community partners.

  • I make complex information understandable

    Through maps, charts, reports, and writing, I turn research into something people can understand and use.

About me

Hi, I'm Isabel!

I'm a geographer and part-time researcher at the University of Toronto, interested in cities, urban life, and the ways people experience place. I write about curious places and ideas on Medium, and outside of GIS and research, I'm usually playing the drums, testing new film on my vintage camera, or trying a new recipe in the kitchen.

I've always been drawn to finding simple, visual ways to make sense of the ideas in my head. GIS brought together that instinct with my interest in cities, giving me a way to explore places through both a technical and creative lens. I love digging into data, breaking complex information down piece by piece, and gradually uncovering the broader spatial patterns within it. Then I turn that research into maps and visual stories that make those patterns easier to see, understand, and connect to place.
